researchTasks: Read the parent issue, blockers, governing product/roadmap documents, current implementation, and recent relevant pull requests before choosing an approach.
Prefer official documentation, primary sources, repository evidence, and measured behavior; record UNKNOWN — REQUIRES VALIDATION instead of inventing facts or permissions.
Treat Sekai Viewer as engineering evidence for rapid vertical slices and data/UI separation, not as proof that extracted data or assets are permitted for this project.
setupSteps: Work from a clean isolated branch using the repository naming convention; install pinned prerequisites and run the documented baseline checks.
List affected files, routes, catalog records, generated artifacts, external services, publication status, and required human approvals before implementation.
implementationSteps: Deliver the smallest end-to-end slice that proves the issue outcome; avoid unrelated refactors and speculative infrastructure.
Keep UI, catalog adapters, build-time validation, preserved Rust/WASM work, preview deployment, approved-data integration, and public-release activation independently testable.
uiUxTasks: Cover normal, loading, empty, error, offline, keyboard, responsive, zoom, reduced-motion, missing-media, unknown, and preview-status behavior where applicable.
Use the approved original design system; do not copy Sekai Viewer, official Arcaea UI, another wiki layout, official branding, or protected assets.
dataBackendTasks: Before `lowiro-publication-authorization` approves a scope, use only synthetic records, project-authored prose, and project-authored or compatibly licensed neutral placeholders.
Do not add real Arcaea metadata, official media/text, extracted resources, scraping/datamining, or an upstream database/API dependency before authorization.
Route components consume typed repository/view-model interfaces; synthetic and later approved-source adapters must remain replaceable.
Do not introduce a hosted backend or database until measured requirements and a separate approved decision justify it.
soloExecution: Execute in this order: evidence → decision/design note → failing test/check → minimal implementation → focused verification → full applicable checks → PR evidence → human review.
Split independently reviewable discoveries into linked follow-up issues instead of silently expanding scope.
validationSteps: Run the narrowest relevant test first, then all checks required by changed files; code or automation changes require `pnpm check`.

Roadmap changes also require shell syntax checks, roadmap tests, and a live read-only dry-run; inspect the plan for unexpected title, body, label, milestone, parent, dependency, assignee, state, or new-issue changes.
Record exact commands and observed results; do not claim checks, permissions, deployment behavior, or source review that was not actually performed.
deliverables: A focused pull request with intentional commits, an acceptance-criteria-to-evidence checklist, changed-surface inventory, and explicit scope cuts.
A concise decision record covering rejected alternatives, residual risks, ownership, next dependency, rollback, AI assistance, and human verification.
risksAndRollback: Synthetic preview, written authorization, approved-data integration, and public release are separate states; never infer a later state from completion of an earlier one.
Silence is not permission. On uncertainty, omit the real content, retain synthetic placeholders, and keep public indexing/release disabled.
Rollback by reverting the focused change and restoring the last validated synthetic or permission-approved app/catalog/asset/deployment snapshot.

implementationSteps: Maintain two tracks: product implementation proceeds on synthetic data; publication proceeds through authorization, approved-source integration, audit, QA, and explicit activation.
validationSteps: Audit the full issue graph to ensure permission gates block real content/public release but do not block shell, UI, schemas, synthetic pages, or controlled preview.

researchTasks: Confirm the minimum contracts needed to start foundation work; do not require completed publication authorization before synthetic implementation.
implementationSteps: Close the gate when product, UI, static adapter, synthetic schema, and pre-permission rules are sufficient for Week 2.
deliverables: Week 1 gate report with allowed/prohibited pre-authorization work and Week 2 readiness.

implementationSteps: Define the application-facing catalog repository interface first, then synthetic implementation, generated view models, compatibility rules, and future approved-source adapter seam.
validationSteps: Prove the same representative route can render from two fixture adapters without route-level data-source knowledge.

researchTasks: Review current lowiro/Arcaea policies and the exact planned prototype scope, but defer the permission request until representative synthetic routes and field inventory exist.
implementationSteps: Write synthetic-only development rules, future source/permission contracts, controlled-preview wording, request-package requirements, correction/takedown flow, and human gates.
validationSteps: Audit synthetic song, character, story, topic, and placeholder records for accidental real-world resemblance, copied expression, misleading labels, and permission ambiguity.
deliverables: Pre-permission policy, prohibited-content list, source/permission convention, preview notice, request-package checklist, correction/takedown path, and maintainer decision.

setupSteps: Prepare invented names, values, relationships, URLs, prose, and original placeholder assets that cannot be mistaken for Arcaea records.
implementationSteps: Model generic domain capabilities and review/provenance states without encoding raw game-dump shapes or speculative Sekai Viewer fields.
validationSteps: Add fixtures that fail on protected-content markers, duplicate IDs, broken references, unsafe URLs, unreviewed assets, oversized prose, and non-synthetic pre-authorization records.

implementationSteps: Sequence quality gate → build migration → design system → shell → synthetic catalog loader → original placeholder pipeline.
validationSteps: Prove one versioned synthetic record renders through the production shell under deployment base-path conditions.

implementationSteps: Use neutral public theme labels Light, Dark, and System and media-independent components.
validationSteps: Review showcase states with long synthetic labels, no media, spoilers, provenance, uncertainty, errors, keyboard, narrow widths, high zoom, and reduced motion.

implementationSteps: Build a domain-neutral shell and preview-status surface; keep domain labels supplied by view models/configuration instead of hard-coded official terminology.
validationSteps: Smoke-test every route with synthetic, loading, missing, not-found, and unavailable states.

implementationSteps: Implement `SyntheticCatalogRepository` first and retain the interface needed by a future approved source adapter.
validationSteps: Test deterministic generation, corrupt/missing/unsupported manifests, adapter substitution, base-path loading, and last-good snapshot recovery.

implementationSteps: Start with project-authored geometric placeholders and explicit authorship records; make permission status a required publication input.
validationSteps: Reject unknown ownership, checksum drift, unsafe paths, oversized output, missing alt decisions, and any pre-authorization official/extracted asset.

implementationSteps: Prioritize a complete synthetic home → explore → detail vertical slice over broad page count.
deliverables: Stable controlled-demo build, route screenshots, field inventory, state matrix, and prototype evidence for lowiro.

implementationSteps: Use synthetic highlights and a prominent pre-authorization/prototype notice; do not imitate a live Arcaea news feed.
Build generic song/collection view models and source/status sections; postpone Arcaea terminology and real metadata mapping to approved integration.
validationSteps: Test complete, minimal, unknown, missing-media, broken-related, and future/unavailable synthetic records.

implementationSteps: Complete reusable synthetic character, story, and topic templates and assemble the permission-request prototype package.
deliverables: Route/field/media inventory, screenshots, exclusions, hosting model, and demonstrated correction/takedown controls.

implementationSteps: Use wholly original synthetic prose; ensure later real-story integration can remain index/facts-only if permission excludes text.
Use invented mechanics and generic topic taxonomy; do not publish World Mode, Course Mode, or other Arcaea-specific explanations before approval.
Harden the synthetic prototype and prepare controlled-preview controls rather than treating quality completion as release permission.
Treat catalog, generated assets, external URLs, Markdown, CI inputs, and any later upstream adapter as untrusted.
validationSteps: Test unsafe URL/HTML/path/SVG/manifest fixtures, secret exposure, action permissions, and generated public artifacts.

implementationSteps: Generate useful metadata but enforce noindex/no public sitemap for the synthetic pre-authorization preview.
validationSteps: Inspect built HTML/metadata/robots/canonical/social outputs for real-game claims, spoilers, unapproved media, and accidental indexing.

implementationSteps: Sequence controlled preview → lowiro request/decision → approved-source integration → content audit → QA → community readiness → explicit public activation.
validationSteps: Reject any plan that lets deployment, QA, or repository visibility bypass authorization or activation.

implementationSteps: Deploy a synthetic, clearly labeled, non-indexed preview with immutable artifact identification and rollback.
validationSteps: Inspect the deployed output for real Arcaea data/media, indexing, direct-link failures, leaked debug routes, and rollback readiness.

researchTasks: Review official contact requirements and prepare a field-level, route-level, host-level proposal based on the implemented prototype.
implementationSteps: Request written decisions separately for naming, factual metadata, descriptions, links, APIs/files/database access, media, caching, transformation, open-source publication, hosting, attribution, and revocation.
validationSteps: Have the maintainer verify the request and interpret the response; preserve raw correspondence privately and record only appropriate redacted evidence.
deliverables: Prototype package, sent-request evidence, redacted decision summary, condition matrix, expiration/revocation controls, and maintainer approval.
risksAndRollback: A rejection or no response keeps real-data integration and public activation blocked while preserving the synthetic product.

setupSteps: Freeze the authorization decision and exact approved field/media/source scope before writing the adapter.
implementationSteps: Map the approved upstream source behind the existing repository contract, normalize at build time, produce diffs/snapshots, and retain synthetic fixtures.
validationSteps: Test unauthorized-field rejection, source outages, malformed responses, duplicates, broken references, attribution, version drift, deterministic output, and rollback.
deliverables: Approved-source adapter, mapping document, normalized snapshot, generated diff, source/permission records, tests, update runbook, and rollback evidence.

implementationSteps: Freeze and audit the exact approved release candidate, not the synthetic preview or an unfrozen upstream source.
validationSteps: Verify every data category and asset against the authorization matrix, source/permission records, generated counts/checksums, rendered pages, and public output.

implementationSteps: Run full release-candidate acceptance after approved integration and content audit; report go/no-go evidence without activating release.
validationSteps: Check route/content regression, accessibility, responsive, performance, security, SEO, legal scope, source/asset integrity, deployment, and rollback against immutable versions.

implementationSteps: Perform final human authorization-scope review, switch robots/sitemap/canonicals and release messaging, and record the exact activated versions only after a go decision.
validationSteps: Re-fetch the deployed site, verify indexing/public metadata state, smoke-test primary flows, compare hashes/versions, and execute or dry-run rollback.
deliverables: Signed go/no-go record, activated deployment evidence, version inventory, public notice, correction/takedown contact, and rollback target.
risksAndRollback: Any ambiguity, expired/revoked permission, audit failure, or QA blocker produces no-go and preserves the synthetic/private state.
